# Keyboard shortcuts

Shortcuts work anywhere in the app, including the prompt box, except as noted under Good to know.

![The Keyboard shortcuts dialog](/screenshots/shortcuts.png)

## How to use

1. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>/</kbd> (<kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>/</kbd> on a Mac) to open the **Keyboard shortcuts** dialog.
2. Type in **Filter by name or key** to find one.
3. Click **Edit** next to it and press the new keys. <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> removes the shortcut.
4. The reset button next to a changed shortcut brings back the default. **Reset all** resets every one.
5. Your changes are kept in this browser only.

| --- | --- | --- |

| Command palette (second key) | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd> | <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>⇧</kbd> <kbd>P</kbd> |
| Open file | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd> | <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>P</kbd> |
| Open settings | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> | <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>,</kbd> |
| Keyboard shortcuts | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>/</kbd> | <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>/</kbd> |
| Go to notifications | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd> | <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>N</kbd> |

## Prefix key

Press <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> (like tmux), let go, then press one more key within 1.5 seconds:

| Then press | Does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>c</kbd> | New session |
| <kbd>n</kbd> | Next tab |
| <kbd>p</kbd> | Previous tab |
| <kbd>1</kbd> … <kbd>9</kbd> | Tab 1 to 9 (9 = last tab) |
| <kbd>x</kbd> | Close tab |
| <kbd>t</kbd> | Terminal |
| <kbd>f</kbd> | Files |
| <kbd>g</kbd> | Changes |
| <kbd>s</kbd> | Sidebar |
| <kbd>z</kbd> | Focus prompt |
| <kbd>,</kbd> | Settings |
| <kbd>?</kbd> | Shortcuts |
| <kbd>:</kbd> | Command palette |

## In the prompt box

These are fixed (not in the registry).

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Send (while Claude works: steer, see [The prompt box](../features/prompt-box)) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> | New line |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> | Next permission mode |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Stop the running turn |
| <kbd>!</kbd> at the start | Bash mode: the line runs as a shell command |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> / <kbd>I</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd> | Bold / italic / inline code (<kbd>⌘</kbd> on a Mac) |

## Good to know

- On Windows and Linux some keys use <kbd>Alt</kbd> because the browser keeps <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>1</kbd>…<kbd>9</kbd> for itself.
- The recorder refuses keys that would break typing: a key without <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>, <kbd>Cmd</kbd> or <kbd>Alt</kbd>, AltGr characters, macOS Option characters, and the prompt box's editing keys (copy, paste, undo, word jumps).
- <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> toggles the sidebar, except in the prompt box, where it makes text bold.
- In the terminal panel, plain <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+letter keys go to the shell. Shortcuts with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, the tab keys, the palette, the shortcuts dialog and the terminal keys still reach the app.
